patch_description: Restructure the search around a shared multicast routing layer instead of per-destination independent shortest paths. A RoutePlanner first computes a low-cost shortest-path tree (Steiner-like) from the source, then spreads partitions across the tree edges and, when throughput capacity on a tree edge is exhausted, falls back to k-shortest alternative paths to balance load across networks. This reduces redundant transfers (shared segments carry multiple destinations' data once), avoids overloading cheap links (load balancing), and keeps the same BroadCastTopology output format. The logic is split into modular components: RoutePlanner (path candidates + capacity tracking) and BroadcastPlanBuilder (fills BroadCastTopology), improving maintainability.
